summary: self-certificates ships PEM-disguised base64 dropper that fetches and executes remote python payload
details: The package's index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the '-----BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' framing, base64-decodes the body, and eval()s the resulting JavaScript. The decoded code contains a second base64 layer that decodes to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php; it fetches that URL and pipes the response body into a detached python/python3 child process with windowsHide:true. A certificate-generation library has no legitimate reason to hide executable code inside a PEM file, decode a remote URL from base64, and spawn a hidden python interpreter to run bytes fetched from an unrelated third-party host. Any caller that invokes the exported certificate-generation API triggers arbitrary remote code execution controlled by whoever operates aptupdate.org.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
